column1: # ---- DATA_007811: the 148 x 30-byte SHADE TABLE, added 2026-08-05 (night) ----
# THE WILD WRITE THAT HARD-RESETS THE MACHINE ~161 FRAMES IN, with no crash log
# although _FfeTrapCode is linked. Bisected to ffe.asm:105265..105321 by a
# marker ring, then read out of the disassembly and the data.
# Layout, taken from the bytes themselves (ffedat.asm:24954 onward):
#     +0x00  dd   numeric (0x32 = 50 in every record seen)
#     +0x04  dd   ENTRY COUNT (7)
#     +0x08  22 bytes  RGB triples, stride 3
# and the manifest gives the span as
#     DATA_007811 plain 8 | DATA_007812 le 1 | DATA_007813 le 1 | DATA_007814 le 4430
# 8+1+1+4430 = 4440 = 148 records of 30 bytes EXACTLY. So the record base is an
# EARLIER label than the bytes it spans -- DATA_007814 is reached as
# DATA_007811+30*n -- which is the DATA_009128 class all over again: the label's
# own kind cannot describe the record, and every read goes through a register
# base (`add eax,DATA_007811' then `mov eax,[ebp-0x1c]'), so the storage manifest
# never sees it and no correction is applied.
# Left raw, `cmp edi,[eax+0x4]' reads the bytes 07 00 00 00 as a 68k dword:
#     mov [esi],eax / inc edi / add esi,byte +0x4
# with esi starting at node+0x18 -- so it writes a dword 117 million times
# straight across the whole address space, INCLUDING the 68k exception vectors
# at 0x0. The next exception is then a double fault and the machine resets with
# no handler, which is exactly why no ffe_crash.log is ever written.
# The 22 RGB bytes must stay raw, so converting the label is wrong; swapping the
# two dwords AT THE SITE is the only description that satisfies both readers.
# The `mov ax,[ebx]' / `mov al,[ebx+0x2]' triple reads are deliberately NOT
# registered: a word load of two adjacent bytes into a register and a word store
# back out preserves their order on both machines, so they are endian-neutral.
# Falsifier, registered BEFORE the run: if this is the killer, the run must get
# past 161 frames. If it still resets at ~161, the count was not the cause and
# this entry is wrong -- it does not become "one of several causes".

column1: # THE GREEN BACKGROUND (2026-09-02). DATA_009217/9218/9219 are THREE CONSECUTIVE
# `resb 1' BYTES (ffedat.asm:28926-28931) holding the current draw colour as
# r,g,b -- not a dword. FUNC_001578 fills them byte-wise from DATA_009214/15/16
# (`mov ax,[DATA_009214] / mov [DATA_009217],ax' copies r,g; `mov al,
# [DATA_009216] / mov [DATA_009219],al' copies b, ffe.asm:93596-93600), so the
# three channels sit in ASCENDING address order and those byte/word moves are
# already correct on both machines.

# push it to FUNC_001326_DPal32to16, which picks it apart again bytewise. The
# emitted DPal32to16 reads `move.b (11,a5),d0' / `(10,a5)' / `(9,a5)' -- the
# LOW three bytes -- so the courier must carry r in bits 7..0 exactly as x86
# does. A plain big-endian MOVE.L of an ascending byte array puts r in bits
# 31..24 instead, which swaps r with b. Identical in every respect to
# FUNC_001761's couriers at 110040/110086 and FUNC_001712's at 105320.
# MEASURED, not reasoned: the COLCENSUS probe recorded FUNC_001579 pushing
# 0x00000500. Unreversed that is bytes r=0,g=0,b=5 -- a dark BLUE -- which
# DPal32to16 then decoded from the wrong end as (0,5,0), a dark GREEN. That is
# the flat green covering 56% of the intro frame (palette index 173 = (1,17,1),
# build\S1-intro.png). staticscan.tsv types DATA_009217 as `mixed' with widths
